To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
miRNAs and novel food compounds are related to the browning process.
miRNAs and dietary compounds can be applied to induce browning in WAT and thus, could contribute to the management of obesity.

1) the miRNAs miR-133 and miR-143 are involved in the regulation of thermogenesis in brown and beige adipocytes, 2) miR-133a-3p is involved in the regulation and activation of beige adipocytes in white adipose tissue, and 3) the food compounds caffeine and capsaicin are able to induce browning/beigine through the modulation of miR-133.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of miRNAs and the effects of food compounds related to browning process.
the identification of miRNA targets that could be involved in the browning/beigening of WAT and with the identification of food compounds that could influence the expression of these miRNAs.
the identification of novel miRNAs and their targets, as well as food compounds that could promote the process of adipose tissue browning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
miRNAs and novel food compounds could represent an interesting strategy to promote adipose browning and to combat obesity.
miRNAs and novel food compounds related to the browning process are a novel and promising approach for obesity prevention and treatment.
there is no evidence of the existence of miRNAs and/or food compounds related to the brown process, although there is evidence of miRNAs related to the beige process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
miRNAs could represent a promising target for the management of obesity through the browning/beigening process.

the browning of WAT is a complex process, and the miRNAs and novel food compounds related to the browning process could be applied in a nutritional strategy for the treatment of obesity and its associated comorbidities.

miRNAs and specific food compounds could be used as potential tools in the fight against obesity.
the use of food compounds and miRNAs could be an effective strategy to combat obesity by promoting browning in WAT.
